To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observed suppression of high transverse momentum jets and photons, together with their correlations, can be understood in terms of jet-quenching in hot QGP, as predicted by the AMY formalisms, and that a consistent description of the experimental data can be achieved by combining jet-quenching with a hydrodynamic model.
1) Jet energy loss in the AMY model, consistently incorporating induced gluon emission as well as elastic scattering, is in good quantitative agreement with RHIC data.

1) the interaction between hard partons and the soft medium in relativistic nuclear collision is essential for the interpretation of jet quench, 2) the interaction between high-pT photons and the soft medium plays a significant role for the understanding of photon production, and 3) the interplay between hard parton energy loss and high-pT photon production in relativistic nuclear collsions can be used to extract the transport coefficients of the medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of hard partons with the soft medium in relativistic nuclear collision.
the study of the interaction of high energy partons (jets) with a dense medium (quark-gluon-plasma).
the interaction between hard partons and the thermal QGP, as it can be studied at RHIC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

jet quenching is not only an important tool for the understanding of the hot quark-glasma medium created in relativistic heavy ion collisions, but also a key to understanding the properties of the medium itself.
the current data are consistent with the picture of jet quenchings and photon production in a thermal QGP medium.
the current experimental data on high p T photons and photon-hadrons correlations are consistent with the presence of a hot quark-guon plasma at RHIC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved a consistent description of the experimental data on photon and jet production in heavy ion collisions at RHIC.

the observed suppression of high-p T hadrons and high-p T direct photons in Au+ Au collisions at RHIC can be understood in a consistent framework, which is a consequence of the formation of a hot and dense QGP in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC energies.
the hot QCD medium at RHIC is indeed a strongly coupled system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high p T photon production is not only a probe for the temperature profile of the medium, but it is also a probe for the jet-medium interaction.
a consistent treatment of the medium response to jets and of the jet-medium interaction is necessary to achieve a satisfactory description of high p T observables in heavy-ion collisions.
the high pT photon data provide an independent, and very useful, handle on the energy loss of high pT jets in heavy ion collisions.
